title: Safety symbols and hazard signs
competency: Identify laboratory hazard signs and safety symbols and say what each one means.

keywords.def: Signs posted in a laboratory that warn of dangers such as poison, fire, electricity or germs.
Signs that show what to wear or do to stay safe, such as gloves or hand wash.
Items you wear to protect yourself in the lab, such as goggles, gloves, a lab coat and boots.
Poisonous. It can harm or kill if swallowed, breathed in or touched.
Chemicals that burn skin and eyes or eat away metals.

en.text: A lab can hold dangerous chemicals, living samples, sharp tools and breakable things. Hazard signs are posted to warn of these dangers. For example, toxic means poisonous. Corrosives burn skin and eyes. Flammable materials catch fire easily. Read the sign before you touch anything.

am.text: ቤተ ሙከራ አደገኛ ኬሚካሎችን፣ ሕያው ናሙናዎችን እና ስለታም መሣሪያዎችን ሊይዝ ይችላል። የአደጋ ምልክቶች ስለ እነዚህ አደጋዎች ያስጠነቅቃሉ። መርዛማ ማለት መርዝ ነው። ተቀጣጣይ ነገሮች በቀላሉ እሳት ይይዛሉ።

screens.title: A sign on the road
screens.text: A fuel tanker drives from Djibouti to Addis Ababa. On its back is a red diamond with a black flame.
screens.ask: What do you think the sign warns?
screens.after:
A flame on a sign warns: this catches fire easily.
Fuel like petrol is flammable.
The red diamond tells drivers and fire fighters to keep flames away.
Labs use warning signs like this too. Read on.

screens.title: 1.2.3 Safety symbols and hazard signs
paras: A lab can hold dangerous chemicals and biological specimens. It can also hold sharp or breakable objects.
So safety symbols and signs are posted throughout the lab. They warn of dangers and keep users safe.

screens.title: A) Hazard signs
items: Poison if swallowed, breathed in or touched. Never taste or smell; wear gloves.
Very strong electricity. Keep away; only trained people work near it.
Burn skin and eyes, eat away metals. Wear goggles and gloves; rinse spills with water.
Catch fire easily. Keep away from flames and heat.
Risk of electric shock. Keep water away; never touch damaged wires.
Where chemicals are kept. Enter only with your teacher.
Living things, like bacteria, that spread disease. Handle as taught; wash hands.
Harms the body, like the lungs, over time. Do not breathe in fumes.

screens.title: Warning words
defs: Signs posted in a lab that warn of dangers such as poison, fire, electricity or germs.
Poisonous. It can harm or kill if swallowed, breathed in or touched.
Chemicals that burn skin and eyes or eat away metals.

screens.title: Which sign warns of burns?
screens.ask: Which sign warns that a chemical can burn your skin?
screens.why:
Step 1: chemicals that burn skin and eyes are corrosives.
Step 2: the corrosives sign is a hazard sign: it warns of danger.
Step 3: gloves, hand wash and hearing protection are protective symbols: they tell you what to do.
So the answer is corrosives.
screens.clue: Look at the hazard signs: which one is about burns?

screens.title: Match sign and meaning
screens.text: Hazard signs: match each sign to its meaning.
pairs: Poisonous if swallowed, breathed in or touched
Living things that may spread disease
screens.why:
Toxic materials → poisonous if swallowed, breathed in or touched.
Biological hazard → living things, like bacteria, that may spread disease.
High voltage hazard → very strong electricity.
Flammable materials → catch fire easily.
Each hazard sign warns of one kind of danger.
screens.clue: Tap each hazard sign to see what it means.

screens.title: A bottle with a flame
screens.text: Tigist finds a bottle with a flame symbol on its label. A Bunsen burner is lit nearby.
opts: Keep it away from the Bunsen burner and other flames
screens.ans: Keep it away from the Bunsen burner and other flames
screens.why:
Step 1: a flame symbol means flammable materials.
Step 2: flammable materials catch fire easily.
Step 3: a lit Bunsen burner is nearby.
So Tigist keeps the bottle away from all flames and heat.
Heating it, smelling it or pouring it in the sink are all unsafe.
screens.clue: What does the flame sign warn about?
screens.worked:
Step 1: flame sign → flammable materials.
Step 2: flammable materials catch fire easily.
Step 3: a lit Bunsen burner is a flame.
So keep the bottle away from any flame or heat.

screens.title: Name the danger
screens.ask: Hazard signs: chemicals that burn skin and eyes or eat away metals are called ___.
screens.why:
Look at the hazard signs.
One sign warns that a chemical burns skin and eyes.
The same chemicals also eat away metals.
That sign is corrosives.
So the answer is corrosives.
screens.clue: Look at the hazard signs for burns and metals.

en.text: Hazard signs warn of a danger. Safety symbols show how to protect yourself or where to find help. Gloves protect your hands. Safety glasses protect your eyes. Boots protect your feet. A hand wash sign reminds you to wash. A fire extinguisher sign shows where it is kept.

am.text: የአደጋ ምልክቶች ስለ አደጋ ያስጠነቅቃሉ። የደኅንነት ምልክቶች ራስህን እንዴት እንደምትጠብቅ ያሳያሉ። ጓንት እጅህን ይጠብቃል። የደኅንነት መነጽር ዓይንህን ይጠብቃል። ቦት ጫማ እግርህን ይጠብቃል።

screens.title: On a building site
screens.text: Workers build a new road bridge in Bahir Dar. A blue sign at the gate shows a boot.
screens.ask: What do you think the blue sign tells the workers?
opts: Danger: the ground is on fire
Wear boots to protect your feet here
screens.after:
A blue sign tells you what to wear or do.
This one shows a boot, so: wear boots here.
Boots protect feet from falling objects and sharp things.
Labs use blue symbols like this too. Read on.
screens.best: Wear boots to protect your feet here

screens.title: B) Laboratory safety symbols
items: Protect your hands from chemicals, heat and sharp things.
Protect your eyes from splashes and flying pieces.
Protect your feet from spills and falling objects.
Protects your whole face from splashes.
Wash your hands after lab work.
Shows where it is. Learn its place before you start.
A lab coat covers your skin and clothes.
Protects your ears from very loud noise.

screens.title: Symbols that protect
defs: Signs that show what to wear or do to stay safe, or where to find help.
Items you wear to protect yourself: goggles, gloves, a lab coat and boots.

screens.title: Protect or warn?
screens.ask: Which of these is a protective symbol, not a hazard warning?
screens.why:
Step 1: hazard signs warn of a danger.
Step 2: safety symbols show what to wear or do to stay safe.
Step 3: toxic, biological hazard and high voltage all name a danger.
Step 4: gloves tell you what to wear.
So gloves is the protective symbol.
screens.clue: Hazard signs warn; safety symbols protect or help.

screens.title: Warn or protect?
screens.text: Does each sign warn of a danger, or protect and help you?
items: It warns of things that catch fire.
It warns of germs and living samples.
It shows where help for a fire is.
They can burn skin and eyes.
It reminds you to clean your hands.
screens.why:
Step 1: ask: does the sign name a danger, or something you wear or use?
Step 2: dangers: toxic, flammable, biological hazard, corrosives, high voltage.
Step 3: protect or help: gloves, safety glasses, fire extinguisher, hand wash.
Hazard signs warn of a danger. Safety symbols tell you how to stay safe.
screens.clue: Ask: does the sign name a danger, or something you wear or use?

screens.title: Guard your eyes
screens.ask: Safety symbols: safety glasses protect your ___ from splashes.
screens.why:
You wear glasses over your eyes.
Safety glasses guard them from splashes and flying pieces.
So the answer is eyes.

screens.title: Work is finished
screens.text: Kebede has finished his lab work with a bacteria sample. He is about to leave.
screens.ask: Which symbol tells him what to do now?
screens.why:
Step 1: Kebede worked with bacteria, which can spread disease.
Step 2: germs may be on his hands.
Step 3: the hand wash symbol says: wash your hands after lab work.
So the answer is hand wash.
High voltage and chemical storage warn of other things.
screens.clue: Which symbol is about cleaning after work?
screens.worked:
Step 1: bacteria can spread disease.
Step 2: after lab work, germs may be on your hands.
Step 3: the hand wash symbol reminds you to wash them.
So the answer is hand wash.

test.text: Which sign warns that a chemical can burn your skin?
test.why:
A chemical that burns skin is a corrosive.
The corrosives sign warns of this danger.
Gloves, hand wash and hearing protection are protective symbols, not warnings.
So the answer is corrosives.

test.text: Signs and symbols: match each sign to its meaning.
pairs: Shows where to find help for a fire
Living things that may spread disease
test.why:
Safety glasses → protect your eyes.
Fire extinguisher → shows where to find help for a fire.
Biological hazard → living things that may spread disease.
High voltage hazard → very strong electricity.
The first two protect or help; the last two warn of danger.

test.text: Why labs post signs: lab safety signs warn of possible dangers and keep lab users safe and informed.
test.why:
A lab can hold dangerous chemicals, germs and breakable things.
Signs are posted throughout the lab for this reason.
They warn of dangers and keep users safe.
So the statement is true.
